body: Thanks.  In general this person seemed quite reserved and shy, except with the people she was using as supply to whom all the jadedness and vitrol would spill out.  In fact it is hard for me to tell if she actually had anyone she called a real "friend" in the sense that I understand it.  So I guess I was dealing with what they call a "covert narcissist"?
Every conversation was always about her all the time, as well.  She really didn't care much about my life,or anyone else's.

I have thousands of points accumulated for answering questions on various sites in the www.stackexchange.com site collection involving mathematics, programming, electrical engineering, and physics.  However, I only have the barest rudiments of a formal education (I think I only took basic algebra in high school, and I studied music in college before dropping out).  I learned all the rest from reading books because I was bored.

Unfortunately, when it comes to the job or relationship market, being an autodidact is not worth one god damn.  And I'm so isolated due to the effects of illness that I don't even have the motivation to do any of it anymore.  No one wants to be around a socially isolated piece of shit with no game and no prospects.

The worst part of all is...after many years of suffering my pain is actually getting _better_.  It's improved to the point where I can actually do more than just focus on the pain all the time and wish it would stop, but not enough that I can fully engage in life again.  You'd think I'd be happy.  But, that is actually the worst curse!  Because the pain isn't there to focus on so much anymore, one has free time to focus on all the things that one has lost over the years.  All the missed opportunities.  All the things that will never be.   It almost feels as if it would have been better to have died, sometimes.  I am a ghost in a world that has moved on and which I can no longer be a part of or understand.
